statement: For independent Bernoulli bond percolation on the infinite d-regular tree T_d, d>=3, p_c(T_d)=1/(d-1) and p_u(T_d)=1.
assumptions: Each edge independently open with probability p

source.novelty: Known result, reproduced here; primary bibliographic check pending

proof: The forward cluster is Galton-Watson with Binomial(d-1,p) offspring, and survives iff p(d-1)>1. For such p<1 fix a bi-infinite geodesic. At each vertex select one incident branch outside this geodesic. The events that its connecting edge is closed and its forward open cluster is infinite are independent with the same positive probability. Almost surely infinitely many occur; these infinite clusters lie in pairwise disjoint components off the geodesic. Thus there are infinitely many infinite open clusters for p_c<p<1, and one at p=1.
remaining_gap: This proof uses disjoint components separated by one edge; a general nonamenable Cayley graph need not have any cut edge.

statement: On a countable simple graph with uniformly bounded degree and adjacency l2 norm a>0, if the Bernoulli bond two-point operator at p0<1 has norm M<infinity, then ||T_q||<=M/(1-aM(q-p0)) whenever p0<=q<=1 and aM(q-p0)<1.

source.novelty: Reproduced standard Russo-BK operator continuation, not claimed new

proof: Finite-volume Russo pivotal probabilities are bounded by the two oriented BK products, so (T^H)'<=T^H A_H T^H entrywise. Norm domination and ||A_H||<=a give the scalar differential inequality f'<=af^2 with f(p0)<=M. The resulting bound is uniform over finite induced subgraphs; monotone convergence of finite-path connectivity and bounded bilinear forms provide the infinite-volume kernel.
remaining_gap: At p0=p_c the required critical norm M is not established for general nonamenable Cayley graphs.

statement: For independent Bernoulli bond percolation on an infinite countable vertex-transitive simple graph of bounded degree, boundedness of T_p on l2 rules out almost-sure uniqueness of an infinite cluster; in particular p_2->2<=p_u.
assumptions: p_u=inf{p:almost surely exactly one infinite cluster}
proof: Almost-sure uniqueness and countability/transitivity give theta>0. FKG yields tau_p(x,y)>=theta^2 for all vertices. Thus every kernel column has infinite squared l2 norm. Entrywise monotonicity makes the bounded-parameter set downward closed, yielding the threshold inequality.
remaining_gap: Combining this with L02 requires finite critical operator norm; this estimate remains unproved here in the general target.

statement: Pointwise exponential decay tau_p(x,y)<=C exp(-c dist(x,y)) with c>0 does not imply l2 operator boundedness. Also, using normalized random-walk rho, pc<1/rho is not the adjacency-Neumann criterion, and its proposed obstruction pc>=1/rho is impossible when rho<1.
counterexample: tau=p^dist; the squared norm of the root column equals 1+4p^2 sum_{n>=0}(3p^2)^n and diverges at p=3/4 since 3p^2=27/16. On T_4, pc=1/3<1/rho but pc>1/(4rho).
remaining_gap: Refutes insufficient estimates only; the parent conjecture is neither disproved nor solved.

statement: For an infinite countable vertex-transitive simple graph of bounded degree, independent Bernoulli bond percolation satisfies pc<pu if pc<1/||A||2->2. For a d-regular graph this condition is pc*d*rho<1 with rho the normalized random-walk spectral radius.
assumptions: Simple graph with uniformly bounded degree
proof: The simple-path union bound is dominated by sum p^n A^n, a bounded Neumann series for pa<1. Choose pc<p<min(1,1/a); T_p is bounded and L03 rules out uniqueness. Thus pc<pu.
remaining_gap: The scalar criterion fails on T_4 despite its nonuniqueness interval; proving it universally is an invalid route.
